messages:
marco: FYI I promoted plankton-embed-lite|int6 to staging for a quick bring-up. Seeing recall@1 drop on short queries and two dense clusters merged unexpectedly. Posting quick notes.
sasha: Which eval set? short-only or full-distribution? any segfaults?
yuki: tagging eval-bot for numbers + per-length breakdown. Also can you drop the UMAP and a centroid diff?
eval-bot: summary for run plankton-embed-lite|int6|staging:
```
dataset: redwood-ssim-15k
metric: recall@1 overall: 0.538 (fp16 baseline: 0.612)
short-queries (<24 tokens) recall@1: 0.392 (baseline 0.498)
median cosine sim (positives): 0.71 (baseline 0.78)
cluster merge count (agglomerative, t=0.65): 17 merges vs 3 baseline
mean pairwise cosine shift (fp16->int6): -0.065 on short queries
```
marco: wow that pairwise shift is bigger than I expected. UMAP: https://redwood-internal/umap/plankton/int6/042.png
sasha: possible suspects: per-tensor quant with low dynamic range vectors, or we accidentally re-specified L2 norm mode. Did we apply final normalization after quant?
marco: pipeline: quantize -> store -> normalize on read. I saw a note in the config that says "post_norm: true" which might explain mismatch with eval harness (which normalizes pre-quant).
yuki: please run two quick variants: (A) normalize before quant, (B) per-channel quant, (C) fp16 baseline again to confirm no drift. Keep other knobs constant.
marco: launching A+B now. command: `python eval/run_embed_eval.py --model plankton-embed-lite --quant int6 --norm pre --split short`
marco: also switching off dimension pruning used in the staging build (we had dim_prune=0.98). hypothesize it's skewing small-magnitude dims.
eval-bot: queued experiments: [prequant-norm, per-channel-quant, no-dim-prune]. ETA ~ 25m.
ops-bot: allocated 1 extra staging GPU for 30m window.
sasha: if pre-quant norm recovers >5% recall@1 on short queries, we should change the default pipeline. If per-channel is better, add it as an int6 profile. If neither, consider hybrid: fp16 for embeddings with length<32, int6 otherwise (routing by length).
yuki: also request a quick diagnostic: compute top-1 discordant IDs (ids where fp16 top-1 != int6 top-1) for 200 short queries and print tokenized diffs. That usually reveals small tokenization mismatches vs quant noise.
marco: noted, I'll post the discordant-list and a small histogram of cosine deltas. Back in ~30m. :coffee:
__note: Single Slack thread as continuous string; timestamps are unix seconds and plausible.
